expected_noise_elements: Project Gutenberg boilerplate start marker: '*** START OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK 84 ***' as the very first line

A CONTENTS/table-of-contents block (lines 9-40) listing 'Letter 1' through 'Letter 4' and 'Chapter 1' through 'Chapter 24' -- IMPORTANT: this ToC lists 28 total entries, but this excerpt's actual body text only goes through Chapter 7 (see review note below) -- a naive implementation might treat the ToC as ground truth for the document's heading count and over-report expected headings that don't actually appear in the body
notes_for_implementer: TRUNCATION DISCLOSURE (important, not a defect in Pith): this fixture's input.txt is intentionally/unavoidably INCOMPLETE -- it was captured via a web-fetch tool with a hard truncation cap during the research phase and ends mid-sentence ('...I saw the lightning playing on the summit of Mont Blanc in') partway through Chapter 7, even though the book's own CONTENTS listing promises Letters 1-4 and Chapters 1-24. This is disclosed prominently here and in notes.md precisely so nobody mistakes the missing Chapters 8-24 for a Pith bug -- Pith is only being asked to normalize the text that is actually present in input.txt (Letters 1-4 + Chapters 1-7, ending mid-word), and expected_headings above lists only those actually-present headings. Separately, this fixture is a good real-world test of the general phenomenon where a document's own table-of-contents promises more structure than the (possibly truncated, possibly corrupted) body actually delivers -- Pith's heading extraction should reflect the actual body content, not blindly mirror the ToC's list of 28 entries.
